_what_this_is: The committed measurement record behind README.md's Performance table (ADR-0042 D7). Every absolute figure published there is bound to an entry here, and PerformanceTableCoherenceTests fails the build when the two disagree. This file is the record; README.md is the claim. When they differ, the claim moves — unless a re-measurement says otherwise, in which case this file moves in its own reviewed commit.
_this_is_not_the_regression_gate: Correspondence between document and record is this file's job. Regression protection is Tests/Verbara.Sdk.Benchmarks/baseline.json, which holds HOSTED-RUNNER means and is a different measurement on different hardware. The two are separate failures and are detected separately (ADR-0042 D4 vs D7).

measurement.note: Three rows are exceptions to the header above, each stated per row rather than hidden behind a single header. The AMI row's post-patch figure was taken on .NET 10.0.6 with MediumRunJob (30 samples), recorded in benchmark-analysis.md section 1.1. rows.note: Fact+Stopwatch against local Docker, not BenchmarkDotNet — the table header does not describe this row's instrument, date or runtime, which is why the row carries its own provenance and README.md states it under the table. Re-measured 2026-09-12: since the 2026-04-18 figures this row published until then, p50 moved 79 µs → 30 µs and batch 65,738 → 91,021 sess/sec, so README understated single saves ~2.6× and batch ~1.4×. In between, the Redis store changed only in rebrand and docs commits and the Redis Fact only in the rebrand; its fixture moved to the Testcontainers 4.11 constructor API (b9c3fa24), outside the timed loop. StackExchange.Redis moved 2.12.14 → 3.1.13, a major version, which is a plausible cause of the movement and not a verified one: no A/B against the old client was run, and the runtime, Docker and kernel moved too. docs/guides/session-store-backends.md:179 publishes ~250 µs for the same measurement where the record has 30 µs, and is wrong.

rows.record_ref: benchmark-analysis.md:391 (2026-09-12 addendum, medians), runs at :379, derivation at :424, WAL-flush proof at :426
rows.note: Re-measured 2026-09-12 on the NpgsqlExecutor store that replaced Dapper, which is what moved this row out of deferred_rows. Fact+Stopwatch against local Docker, not BenchmarkDotNet. Single-save latency is bound by the measuring machine's WAL flush, not by SDK code: one SaveAsync is one autocommit UPSERT and so one fdatasync, measured at 2002 µs/op on the same storage, and single-row inserts run 499 tps with synchronous_commit=on against 116,739 tps with it off (proof at benchmark-analysis.md:426). That is why p50 1.97 ms did not move across the rewrite, and why section 1c's attribution to JSONB parsing and indexes is wrong. Batch rose 9,491 → 13,489 sess/sec since 2026-04-18; that delta is NOT attributable to the Dapper removal: the runtime (10.0.5 → 10.0.12), PostgreSQL (16 → 18), Npgsql (10.0.2 → 10.0.3), Docker and the kernel all moved over the same period, and Redis, whose store code did not change, moved by a comparable or larger factor too. docs/guides/session-store-backends.md:9-11 publishes Postgres read latency as 5-10 ms where the record has GetAsync p50 = 48 µs (benchmark-analysis.md:391); that divergence is separate from the store rewrite and still open.
